name: Complex Vascular Malformation with Associated Anomalies

criteria.description: Presence of two or more types of vascular malformations (capillary, venous, lymphatic, arterial) in a single patient
Presence of associated anomalies such as soft tissue hypertrophy, limb asymmetry, or skeletal abnormalities
Radiological evidence of complex vascular malformations on MRI, ultrasound, or angiography
Identification of pathogenic variants in genes associated with vascular malformations (if available)

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of multiple vascular malformation types with associated anomalies confirmed by imaging
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is primarily clinical supported by imaging; genetic testing may aid but is not mandatory.

pathognomonic.notes: Visible complex vascular lesions involving multiple vessel types

pathognomonic.symptomName: Soft tissue hypertrophy associated with vascular malformations

searchTerms: one limb larger than the other

common.symptomName: Pain localized to vascular malformation sites
searchTerms: pain at blood vessel malformation sites

common.symptomName: Skin discoloration with bluish or reddish hue
searchTerms: skin with blue or red tint
open sores over blood vessel areas

rare.symptomName: High-output cardiac failure secondary to large arteriovenous shunting
searchTerms: heart failure from abnormal blood flow
heart problems due to blood vessel shunts

rare.symptomName: Neurological deficits due to intracranial vascular malformations
searchTerms: nerve problems from brain vessel malformations

rare.symptomName: Deep vein thrombosis in affected limbs

laboratory: Normal or mildly elevated D-dimer levels
Possible anemia secondary to chronic bleeding
imaging: MRI demonstrating mixed vascular malformations with characteristic flow voids
Doppler ultrasound showing abnormal vascular channels and flow patterns
genetic: Pathogenic variants in genes such as TEK, PIK3CA, or RASA1 (if tested)
other: Histopathology showing abnormal vessel morphology with combined vessel types

distinguishingFeatures: Classic triad of capillary malformation, venous malformation, and limb hypertrophy
Usually involves lower limbs with port-wine stains
Multiple venous malformations predominantly affecting skin and gastrointestinal tract

redFlags: Rapid progression of vascular lesion size
Neurological symptoms suggestive of intracranial involvement
references: Orphanet: Complex Vascular Malformation with Associated Anomalies, ORPHA:211277
Mulliken JB, Young AE. Vascular Birthmarks: Hemangiomas and Malformations. Saunders; 1988.
Wassef M, Blei F, Adams D, et al. Vascular anomalies classification: recommendations from the International Society for the Study of Vascular Anomalies. Pediatrics. 2015;136(1):e203-e214.
